objective: For a nearest-neighbour shift of finite type X on the tree of F2 (a value law on a place and its four neighbours over a finite alphabet): (1) a finite board exists iff the balance equations over X's tree patterns have a nonzero nonnegative solution (a linear program); (2) Lemma A'': if some solution has infinitely many pairwise disjoint half-trees each with two completions, X has a solution with trivial stabilizer; (3) L1: a vertex type (pattern, parent direction) that can reach a branching choice and recurs in two different child directions of itself gives such a solution; (4) L2: a solution determining an end (each place with exactly one neighbour one level lower) whose end can be chosen outside the countably many ends fixed by nontrivial elements is free; the horofunction law qualifies; (5) the target W: every infinite such X has a solution with trivial stabilizer, or the gap stated.
title: Free solutions without finite boards
